app.name: Video Frame Expedition
app.fullName: Video Frame Expedition for DaVinci Resolve

library.title: Library
library.subtitle: Your video folders and their analyses
library.removeConfirm: Remove “{{label}}”? Analyses will be deleted; your video files are not touched.
library.emptyBody: Add a folder of footage: the app reads it, describes each video with your local vision model and only writes one small analysis file per video there (can be turned off in System).
library.autoUpdateOn: Automatic update on: the folder is checked every 2 minutes and new videos are analysed.
library.autoUpdateOff: Automatic update off: “Rescan” finds new videos.

addRoot.title: Add a folder
addRoot.description: The folder is read, never modified. All application data is stored separately.
addRoot.pathHelp: Absolute path, for example D:\Videos\Beach shoot
addRoot.label: Display name
addRoot.focusHelp: What matters to you in this footage: subjects, moods, intended use…
addRoot.autoAnalyzeHelp: The folder is watched: videos added or changed are found and analysed with nothing to do.

lmStudio.noVision: No vision model loaded in LM Studio
lmStudio.body: You can add the folder now: its videos will be analysed without the vision model, then completed on their own as soon as it answers. To set LM Studio first, on this computer or another one:

video.analyzeBody: Results already obtained are kept unless you choose to update or redo everything.
video.unsupported: Your browser cannot play this file.
video.keyframesEmpty: No keyframes yet: the analysis is queued or running.
video.selectFrame: Pick a keyframe to see its description.
video.visibleText: Text read by the vision model
video.focusHint: A new or changed focus has the images described again with it.
video.proxyNote: Playing a viewing copy (H.264, corrected colours): {{reason}}. The original stays untouched and is the one analysed.
video.proxyPending: {{reason}}. A viewing copy will be made by the analysis: “Analyse…” then “Complete”.
video.rerunHint: ↻ runs a stage again, with the stages that need its result.
video.rerunConfirmBody: These stages need its result: they will be redone too.
video.rerunHeavy: The vision model or the transcription will be used: this may take several minutes.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.subtitle: Scans and analyses run by the worker
jobs.stopAllBody: What is already analysed is kept; “Analyse” picks up where the analyses stopped.

summary.label: Tasks summary
summary.etaHint_one: Estimated at the pace of the latest analyses: {{pace}} per video, one at a time.
summary.etaHint_other: Estimated at the pace of the latest analyses: {{pace}} per video, {{count}} at a time.

languages.title: Analysis languages
languages.intro: Every analysis exists in French and in English: the interface shows and exports (files, timelines, subtitles) the texts in its own language, chosen in the top-right menu.
languages.writtenHint: The models write the analyses in this language; the “Translation” stage translates them into the other one. Changing it redoes nothing: only the next analyses are written in the new language.
languages.translateHint: The analyses already made are not redone: their texts are translated by the model loaded in LM Studio (about a minute for a two-minute video). New analyses are translated on their own.

analysisFiles.title: Analysis files
analysisFiles.label: Write the analysis file next to the videos
analysisFiles.hint: After each analysis, two small text files named like the video, one per language (“20260812_201337_FR.txt”, and “20260812_201337_EN.txt” once translated; JSON, no images), join the video in its folder, with all its analyses. They are the only files the app writes in your folders (with the subtitles of a timeline made in Resolve); a file of that name it did not write is never replaced, and the former “20260812_201337.txt” it had written is removed.
analysisFiles.note: A video never analysed before that has its analysis file is taken over from it (the images are made again): only what is missing is analysed. This file holds the GPS position and what is said in the video: sharing the folder shares them too.

data.title: Your data
data.help: The library (the videos, their analyses, the frames taken from the videos) and the application's settings are kept in a database, on this computer. Export it to back it up or to take it to another computer, import one, or start afresh.
data.withImages: With the frames taken from the videos ({{size}})
data.withImagesHint: Without them, the archive is much lighter and enough for a backup on this computer; on another one, the library would lose its frames.
data.exportNote: The archive also holds your settings, the saved tokens among them (LM Studio): keep it somewhere safe.
data.exporting: Preparing the archive… (with the frames, this may take a minute)
data.importHint: An export of Video Frame Expedition (.zip), or a database of the backups folder (.sqlite3).
data.keepSettingsHint: Otherwise, the file's ones replace them, the address of LM Studio included.
data.importReady: Import ready: restart the application to apply it.
data.importConfirmBody: At the next start of the application, this computer's library will be replaced by the one in “{{name}}”, its frames too if the file holds them. A copy of the current database will stay with the backups; to be able to get everything back, frames included, export first.
data.resetLibrary: The library: the videos, their analyses, the frames taken from them
data.resetSettings: The application's settings, LM Studio's address included
data.resetHint: Your videos themselves, the subtitles laid in Resolve and the downloaded models are never touched.
data.resetConfirmLibrary: At the next start of the application, the library will be erased: the videos, their analyses and the frames taken from them. The settings stay.
data.resetConfirmSettings: At the next start of the application, the settings will go back to those of a new installation. The library stays.
data.resetConfirmBoth: At the next start of the application, everything will start afresh, as after a new installation: the library (the videos, their analyses, the frames) and the settings will be erased.
data.resetConfirmBackup: A copy of the current database will stay with the backups, but not the frames: to be able to get everything back, export first.
data.resetConfirmCopy: A copy of the current database will stay with the backups.
data.resetReady: Reset ready: restart the application to apply it.
data.pendingNoImages: Without frames: this computer's ones stay.
data.pendingTheirSettings: The file's settings will replace this computer's ones.
data.pendingResetBoth: The library and the settings will be erased.
data.pendingWhen: On restart, the current database is first copied to the backups, and the analyses under way stop.
data.restartHint: The application stops, then starts again in its window; this page reloads by itself, without opening another tab.
data.restartManual: To apply it, stop the application (close its window or press Ctrl+C), then start it again.
data.restarting: Restarting the application… The page will reload by itself.
data.restartLate: The application does not come back: start it again from the Start menu or the Applications folder (“Video Frame Expedition”).
data.lastBackup: The previous database is with the backups: {{file}}.
data.lastFailed: The operation of {{when}} failed: {{error}}. Your data stayed as it was.

errors.not_a_library: This file is neither an export of Video Frame Expedition nor one of its databases.
errors.newer_library: This library comes from a newer version of the application: update this one first (“Video Frame Expedition - update”).

mcp.title: Claude access (MCP)
mcp.label: Allow Claude to add folders to the library
mcp.hint: With analyze_folder, Claude analyses the folders already declared. Turned on, it can also declare a new one (and have it analysed).
mcp.note: Off by default: text read in a video or transcribed speech could ask it to analyse other folders.

hardware.title: Graphics card
hardware.gpu_decodeHint: Faster on 4K videos; only when the vision model leaves enough free memory.
hardware.gpu_transcriptionHint: About 2 to 6 times faster; needs cuBLAS 12 (“vfe models cuda-runtime”) and about 2.6 GB free with Whisper turbo. Otherwise the CPU transcribes as usual.
hardware.note: The vision model loaded in LM Studio comes first: the GPU is lent only when memory allows, with a margin, and given back right after.

visionModel.title: Vision model
visionModel.queued: Calibration requested: a few seconds once it starts
visionModel.noModel: No vision model loaded in LM Studio.
visionModel.unreachable: LM Studio cannot be reached: start its server, then come back.
visionModel.truncated: cut at least once (loop or reasoning)
visionModel.reasoningOn_one: on ({{count}} token): switch it off in LM Studio
visionModel.reasoningOn_other: on ({{count}} tokens): switch it off in LM Studio
visionModel.notCalibrated: not calibrated yet: done at the first analysis

lmstudioLink.title: Model server
lmstudioLink.help: The server whose models describe your frames: LM Studio by default, or a server compatible with OpenAI's API, such as vLLM. On this computer, or on another one of your network (local network, Tailscale), for instance a PC with a more powerful graphics card.
lmstudioLink.thereHint: Another computer, or another model server (vLLM on this computer: 127.0.0.1:8000).
lmstudioLink.addressHint: Its address on your local network or on Tailscale, or its name: 192.168.1.20, 100.64.12.34:1234, living-room-pc. Port 1234 is added when missing. Over there, in LM Studio: Developer › Server Settings › "Serve on Local Network".
lmstudioLink.addressHintOpenai: Its address with its port, for instance gpu-box:8000 or http://192.168.1.20:8000/v1. The port and the path are kept as typed (/v1 when there is no path).
lmstudioLink.tokenHint: Only if this server asks for one (in LM Studio: Developer › Server Settings). It is sent to this address only.
lmstudioLink.tokenKept: A token is saved for this address: leave empty to keep it.
lmstudioLink.parallelHint: vLLM handles requests in batches: 4 to 8 let it describe several frames at once.
lmstudioLink.visionHint: Untick for a server whose models only write text: the analyses then wait for a vision model; Questions still work.
lmstudioLink.privacy: The frames of your videos will be sent to this computer. On a local network they travel unencrypted; Tailscale encrypts them.
lmstudioLink.ok_one: LM Studio answers at {{url}}: {{count}} model, {{vision}} with vision.
lmstudioLink.ok_other: LM Studio answers at {{url}}: {{count}} models, {{vision}} with vision.
lmstudioLink.okOpenai_one: An OpenAI-compatible server answers at {{url}}: {{count}} model, {{vision}} with vision.
lmstudioLink.okOpenai_other: An OpenAI-compatible server answers at {{url}}: {{count}} models, {{vision}} with vision.
lmstudioLink.noneLoaded: No vision model is loaded there.
lmstudioLink.imagesOk: Its vision model did see the test image.
lmstudioLink.imagesRefused: Its model refuses images: untick “This server sees images”, or serve a vision model.
lmstudioLink.pastEmpty: None yet: every saved address is added here.
lmstudioLink.note: The change applies at once, without restarting the application; it is refused while an analysis or a model test is running. The model bench only measures memory for the LM Studio of this computer.

access.loginTitle: Sign in to Video Frame Expedition
access.loginIntro: This device is not the computer running the app: enter the access token to continue.
access.where: Where is it? On the app's computer: the “Connections” page opened at http://127.0.0.1:8765, or the “vfe token” command.

connections.title: Connections
connections.subtitle: Plug Video Frame Expedition into your assistants, here or from your other devices
connections.intro: Video Frame Expedition's MCP server lets an assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor…) consult your analysed videos: find shots, read what is said, look at frames, prepare an edit in DaVinci Resolve. It answers while the app is running, and nothing leaves your devices.
connections.remoteOff: Off. To turn it on, add VFE_TAILSCALE=true to the .env file at the root of the app (or start “run.bat tailscale”), allow the port in Windows Firewall (see the guide), then restart the app.
connections.tokenHelp: Asked of other devices (sign-in page, remote MCP clients). This computer does not need it.
connections.tokenRotate: To change it: “vfe token --rotate”, then restart the app (devices will have to sign in again).
connections.tokenHidden: The token is only shown on the app's computer.
connections.tokenNone: No token yet: it is created at the first start with remote access (or right away with “vfe token”).
connections.clientsHelp: Configurations ready to copy. Once added, the server is called “vfe-vision” in the client.
connections.placeholder: Replace <TOKEN> with the token (“Show” above puts it in the examples).

claudeCode.help: In a terminal (--scope user makes it available in all your projects):

claudeDesktop.help: Claude Desktop only launches local commands: it goes through the “vfe mcp-stdio” bridge shipped with the app, which relays to it without ever starting it. Configuration file:
claudeDesktop.merge: Add the “vfe-vision” entry under “mcpServers”, keeping the rest of the file, then fully quit Claude Desktop (icon near the clock) and start it again.

vscode.help: Command “MCP: Open User Configuration” (or .vscode/mcp.json in a project):
vscode.remoteHelp: VS Code asks for the token once and keeps it in its secret storage.

codex.remoteHelp: Put the token in the {{variable}} environment variable of that device.
codex.stdioHelp: If your Codex version does not take HTTP servers, go through the stdio bridge:

other.httpRemote: From another device, with this header:
other.stdio: stdio transport (the client launches the command):
other.stdioHelp: For an app on another device: --url with its address, and the token with --token or the VFE_MCP_TOKEN variable.

resolve.title: DaVinci Resolve
resolve.help: DaVinci Resolve Studio's MCP (ResolveMCP.exe, stdio) drives Resolve; Video Frame Expedition gives it the shots (find_clips: paths, in and out points, timecodes). Plug both into the same assistant.
resolve.missing: Not found there (DaVinci Resolve Studio 21 or later).

connections.guide: Full guide, Tailscale access and firewall included: docs/guide/connect-mcp.md.

resolveLink.title: Where DaVinci Resolve runs
resolveLink.help: Resolve can run on another computer (a Mac, say) that reads this one's rushes through a network share: the application then reads it remotely and matches the paths.
resolveLink.addressHint: Its name or Tailscale address (100.x.y.z), or its local network address. In Resolve Studio on that computer: Preferences › System › General › External scripting using “Network”.
resolveLink.folders: The same folders seen from both sides
resolveLink.foldersHint: On the left the folder on this computer, on the right the same folder as Resolve sees it (for example D:\cats 2026 and /Volumes/cats 2026).
resolveLink.note: DaVinci Resolve's MCP only drives the Resolve of its own machine: for it, Claude must run on Resolve's computer. The assistant's Resolve tools (below) go through this application: Claude can then stay here. This computer keeps DaVinci Resolve installed (not running) for its scripting library.

resolveTools.title: Resolve tools for the assistant
resolveTools.help: MCP tools that spare Claude writing scripts for Resolve: it reads a timeline tied to the analyses, plans the reframing (the subjects' heads found by the vision model loaded in LM Studio), builds a new timeline and puts the markers, through the application's fixed scripts.
resolveTools.label: Enhanced DaVinci Resolve tools for the assistant
resolveTools.hint: read_timeline, plan_reframe, build_timeline, apply_markers. Claude only sends data (shots, seconds, framings), never code.
resolveTools.note: Off by default. New timelines are named “… - vfe vN”: an existing timeline is never changed, and the project is not saved (Ctrl+S in Resolve if you keep the edit).

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.help: Click to seek. Keyboard: ←/→ 1 s (Shift: 10 s), Page Up/Page Down: previous/next shot.

technique.emptyBody: They will appear when the analysis finishes (“Shots, motion and signals” and “Audio levels” stages).

series.motionHint: optical flow, px per analysed frame

technique.clippingTitle: Share of crushed shadow / clipped highlight pixels

shots.emptyBody: The shot list will appear when the analysis finishes.
shots.caption: Shots of the video

story.title: What happens
story.possibleCutHint: The images seem to show different subjects: a cut may have been missed
story.footnote: Stories generated by {{model}} — may contain errors

capture.title: Shooting and camera

source.export: Only the export date is known
source.nameDate: Day read from the file name
source.nameTime: Date and time read from the file name
source.nameTimeOffset: File name + offset recorded by the phone
source.nameTimeZone: File name, confirmed by the container date

capture.exportedNote: File exported or re-encoded by software: container dates are the export date.
capture.offsetInferred: UTC offset: {{offset}} (inferred from the file name and the container date)
capture.offsetMismatch: The device clock was set to {{offset}}, unlike the time zone of the place.
capture.modelNotRecorded: {{os}} · model not recorded in the file

warning.possible_pause: The recording seems to have been paused: the start comes from the file name.
warning.name_mismatch: The file name does not match the internal dates (renamed file?): the container date is used.

context.mapHidden: Map hidden: online services are off (no tile is requested).
context.noDaylight: No more daylight: artificial light likely
context.windowNote: The capture time is only probable: within ± 30 min the light goes through {{phases}}. No phase is stated.
context.takeNote: During the take, the light goes through {{phases}} (values computed at the start).

comparison.consistent: Measured white balance consistent with natural light.
comparison.warmer: Frames warmer than natural light allows: tungsten, warm LED or grading?
comparison.cooler: Frames cooler than natural light: shade, tungsten preset or screens?

context.offLocus: Twilight: kelvin values are only indicative.

assumption.capture_start: computed at the start of the take

context.weatherCaveat: Weather-model estimate (grid cell {{distance}} away), not an observation: the frames are the judge of the visible sky.
context.offlineNotice: Online services are off: no map, no weather, approximate place.
context.empty: No context: neither a position nor a usable capture time.
context.folderDefault: Folder default position, not the capture position: approximate place.
context.offlineNoticeKept: Online services are off: the data shown comes from an earlier online analysis; no new request is made.

curve.title: Sun elevation through the day (local time)
curve.label: Sun elevation through the day: {{description}}

context.openContext: See the shooting context (place, sun, weather)
context.noGpsTitle: No GPS position in this file
context.noGpsBody: Place, weather and sun elevation are found from the GPS coordinates the device records. This file has none: location turned off in the camera app, or an export from an editing application that does not copy them. On a Galaxy, turn on “Location tags” in the camera settings.

hint.complete: Keeps everything already analysed. Only does what is missing, failed, or whose data changed (time, place, file).
hint.update: Also redoes what was produced with other settings, another model or an earlier version of the app.
hint.full: Redoes every step from scratch. May take a while.

analysisMode.nothingMissing: Nothing is missing: “Complete” will not redo anything.
analysisMode.outdated: Made by an earlier version (kept as is): {{stages}}.
analysisMode.banner: Analyses to complete for this video: {{stages}}.
analysisMode.rootBody: Videos already analysed keep their results unless you choose to update or redo everything.
analysisMode.rootNothing: Nothing to complete: every video in this folder is up to date.

hintChosen.complete: Among the ticked stages, only does what is missing, failed, or whose data changed. Up-to-date videos are left out.
hintChosen.update: Also redoes the ticked stages produced with other settings, another model or an earlier version of the app.
hintChosen.full: Redoes the ticked stages, even successful ones, and the stages that need their results. May take long.

audio.presenceLabel: Share of the duration for each sound family
audio.multiLabel: Sounds can overlap: the shares do not add up.
audio.source: Automatic recognition ({{model}}, AudioSet classes): indicative, especially for faint sounds.
audio.noHeard: No specific sound recognised apart from speech and music.
audio.heardHint: Total duration, then the moments it is heard: click to listen.
audio.cedMissing: Second opinion off: install CED-small with “vfe models sounds”, then “Update”.
audio.heardNotComputed: Sounds heard not computed yet for this video: choose “Update” in “Analyse”.
audio.cedUpdate: CED-small's second opinion is available: “Update” adds it to this video.

transcript.suspect: Unreliable segment (probably hallucinated by the model)
transcript.untrusted: Automatic transcript (Whisper): check proper names and greyed passages.
transcript.noSpeech: No speech detected in this video.
transcript.modeSaved: Saved: the transcription is being redone.

part.previous: The latest analysis did not complete ({{reason}}): previous result shown.

subjects.title: Subjects found
subjects.none: No living being found in this frame.

batch.noVideo: Tick videos in the library to analyse them.

batch.offline_other: {{count}} offline videos (file out of reach) were not analysed.

batch.alsoRedoneIf: If a ticked stage is redone, the stages that need its result are redone too: {{stages}}.

export.notAnalyzed_other: {{count}} videos not analysed yet: nothing to write.

exports.title: Exports
exports.intro: Download this video's analyses in the format you need. Nothing is written next to the video.
exports.note: Texts come from the video and local models: proofread them before publishing. Timecodes: the file's own (00:00:00:00 when it has none).

csv.hint: One shot per row: times, timecodes, camera movement, usability, role, what happens, subjects, speech. Opens in Excel (“;” separator, decimal comma).

resolve.heading: DaVinci Resolve
resolve.open: Open, project “{{name}}”: the timeline can be added to it directly.
resolve.what: It will be created there and opened. Files missing from the media pool are imported into the “Video Frame Expedition” bin, with the timeline.
resolve.whatMarkers: Markers are placed on the media pool clips, which the timeline takes on; yours are left alone.
resolve.whatSubtitles: Subtitles are laid on the timeline, one track per kind, and also written next to each video (<name>_FR.srt for the speech, in the language spoken; <name>_SHOTS_EN.srt for the shots, in the interface's language).
resolve.whatSubtitlesRemote: Subtitles are laid on the timeline, one track per kind, from files written next to its first video (<timeline>_TIMELINE_EN.srt), which DaVinci Resolve's computer reads through the folder pairs; they are also written next to each video (<name>_FR.srt for the speech, in the language spoken; <name>_SHOTS_EN.srt for the shots, in the interface's language).
resolve.fileInstead: You can download the FCPXML file and import it in Resolve: File › Import › Timeline…

timelineBuild.importHint: In DaVinci Resolve: File › Import › Timeline…, then the .otio file of the ZIP (the videos and their markers). Subtitles (.srt) are imported separately: see README.txt.
timelineBuild.markersMissed_one: {{count}} marker could not be placed (past the end of the clip, or no free frame nearby)
timelineBuild.markersMissed_other: {{count}} markers could not be placed (past the end of the clip, or no free frame nearby)

timelineBuild.subtitlesInBin_other: {{count}} subtitle files, written next to their videos, in the “Video Frame Expedition” bin
timelineBuild.subtitlesHint: Drag each one ({{names}}) to the very start of its video on the timeline: the transcript's on one subtitle track, the shots' (_SHOTS) on another. DaVinci Resolve runs on another computer and no folder of the videos could take the timeline's tracks: the application cannot lay them itself.

synthesis.writtenByNoModel: Titles, summaries and reasons written by a language model — may contain errors

search.title: Search
search.subtitle: What is seen, said, heard or read in your videos.
search.label: Search the videos
search.placeholder: A dog in the snow, “sunset”, a spoken word…
search.start: Type words or a description, in French or English: the search reads the image descriptions, the shot stories, speech, on-screen text, sounds and summaries. Filters alone list videos, or shots when a filter is about shots.
search.generated: Excerpts from the analyses: descriptions, stories and transcripts are generated and may be wrong.

empty.title: No results
empty.body: Try other words, a simpler description, or remove filters.

noIndex.title: No video indexed
noIndex.body: The search index is built at the end of each analysis. For videos already analysed, run “Complete” in the library: it is quick, nothing is described again.

search.partial: {{indexed}} of {{videos}} videos indexed: “Complete” in the library indexes the others.
search.wordsOnly: Search by words only: the search-by-meaning model is not installed. Run “vfe models search”, then “Complete” in the library.
search.someVectors: Search by meaning does not cover every video yet: “Complete” in the library adds them.

ask.title: Questions
ask.subtitle: Ask a question about your videos: the model loaded in LM Studio answers from the passages found, and cites its sources.
ask.label: Your question
ask.placeholder: Where did I film a dog in the snow? What is said about the saucepan?
ask.hint: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line. The filters below limit the passages the model reads.

check.label: Visual check
check.hint: The model looks at 1 to 4 images of the cited moments to confirm or correct the answer (slower).
check.noVision: The loaded model does not read images.

ask.start: Answers come only from the analyses of your videos: image descriptions, shot stories, speech, on-screen text, sounds, places, dates and syntheses. Every statement cites its passages; clicking a source opens the video at that moment.

phase.writing: The model is writing the answer…
phase.stopped: Answer stopped: what was written is kept in the history.

status.noAnswer: The passages found do not answer this question.

noPassages.title: No matching passage
noPassages.body: The search found nothing for this question or these filters: the model was not asked. Try other words or remove filters.

status.uncited: This answer cites no passage: it may not come from your videos.
status.truncated: Answer cut: it reached its maximum length.

ask.dropped_one: {{count}} citation of a passage that does not exist was removed.
ask.dropped_other: {{count}} citations of passages that do not exist were removed.
ask.generated: Answer generated by the local model from the analyses: it may be wrong, check the sources.
ask.privacy: Questions and passages only go to the model server chosen on the System page, on this computer or on your local network (VPN included).

noIndex.title: No indexed video

offline.relinkHint: Choose a folder: the files are looked for in it (sub-folders included) by size and content, like DaVinci Resolve's Relink.
offline.relinkStarted_one: Looking for the video in “{{folder}}” (task running).
offline.relinkStarted_other: Looking for the {{count}} videos in “{{folder}}” (task running).

offline.forgetTitle_other: Remove the {{count}} offline videos from the library?

offline.left_other: {{count}} videos left: their file is there, or they are being analysed.

new.noModels: LM Studio has no vision model: download one, then come back here.

new.noFrames: The bench shows the models frames of your library: analyse a video first.
new.tight: May not fit entirely on the card: the test will tell.

new.tooBig_other: {{count}} models larger than the card's memory, which cannot be tested

new.language: Descriptions asked in {{language}}, the language the analyses are written in.

new.restore_other: Loaded models ({{names}}): they will be unloaded for the test, then loaded again with their settings.

new.waiting_other: {{count}} jobs are running: the test starts when they end. The analyses that wait come after it.

help.title: How to read this table
help.vram: Memory: what the model takes on the graphics card once loaded, and what is then left for DaVinci Resolve, decoding and transcription. “Card full”: so little is left that Windows spills into the system memory, and everything slows down.
help.speed: Speed: the time per frame for a description, several requests being sent at a time, as during an analysis.
help.answers: Valid answers: those that follow the requested format. An answer “asked again” had to be corrected by the model; an answer “cut” went over the allowed length.
help.language: Language kept: the descriptions written in the language asked for.
help.text: Text read: the share of the words the application's own text reading found that the model read too. “Unconfirmed”: a text given by the model where the text reading saw none.
help.positions: Positions: the share of the people and animals the application's detector found that the model boxed at the same place, and how precise the calibration is on known shapes (1: perfect boxes).
help.quality: Quality: the mean of your blind ratings, from 0 (wrong) to 3 (right).
help.best: The best value of each column stands out.

blind.title: Blind rating
blind.intro: Look at the frame, then rate each description. The letters change with every frame: you do not know which model wrote what. Your ratings go to the “Quality” column of the table.
blind.failed: No model gave a valid answer for this frame.

note.label: Note on this test
note.placeholder: For example: before the LM Studio update

all.title: General ranking
all.intro_one: The latest result of {{count}} model, all tests together, for descriptions asked in {{language}}.
all.intro_other: The latest result of each of the {{count}} models, all tests together, for descriptions asked in {{language}}.
all.mixed: These tests did not all use the same images: memory and speed compare from one test to another, the rest is indicative.

scatter.title: Memory and speed
scatter.hint: The best corner is the bottom left one: little memory used, little time per image.
scatter.label: Memory used and time per image. {{points}}
scatter.yLog: Seconds per image (logarithmic scale: each mark doubles or more)

rank.title: Ranking
rank.totalHint: Out of 100 points: the mean of the points earned on each measure ({{measures}}).
rank.left_one: {{names}} is left out of the total: not every model has it.
rank.left_other: {{names}} are left out of the total: not every model has them.
rank.profilesHint: One branch per measure, from 0 points at the centre to 100 at the rim: the larger the surface, the better the model.
rank.profileAlone: One branch per measure, from 0 points at the centre to 100 at the rim. The speed is left out: it counts against the fastest model, and it takes at least two models to compare it.

how.title: How the points are worked out
how.vram: Memory: the share of the graphics card the model leaves free. A model that takes a quarter of the card has 75 points.
how.speed: Speed: the fastest model has 100 points; a model twice as slow has 50.
how.shares: Language, text read, positions: the share measured. A model whose positions are disabled has 0.
how.quality: Quality: the mean of your blind ratings, brought to 100.
how.total: Total: the mean of these points. Only the measures every ranked model has are counted, so that all are judged on the same ground; "What matters most" makes one measure count three times.

connections.remoteOff: Off. To turn it on, add VFE_TAILSCALE=true to the .env file at the root of the app (or start “run.command tailscale”), let Python accept incoming connections if macOS's firewall asks (see the guide), then restart the app.

claudeDesktop.merge: Add the “vfe-vision” entry under “mcpServers”, keeping the rest of the file, then fully quit Claude Desktop (Cmd+Q) and start it again.

resolve.help: DaVinci Resolve Studio's MCP (ResolveMCP, stdio) drives Resolve; Video Frame Expedition gives it the shots (find_clips: paths, in and out points, timecodes). Plug both into the same assistant.

resolveLink.foldersHint: On the left the folder on this computer, on the right the same folder as Resolve sees it (for example /Volumes/cats 2026 here and D:\cats 2026 when Resolve runs on a Windows PC).

resolveTools.note: Off by default. New timelines are named “… - vfe vN”: an existing timeline is never changed, and the project is not saved (Cmd+S in Resolve if you keep the edit).

help.vram: Memory: measured on NVIDIA cards only. On a Mac, the model shares the unified memory with DaVinci Resolve and the application, and nothing is measured here.

hardware.gpu_transcriptionHint: No effect on a Mac: transcription stays on the processor (its engine does not use the chip's graphics cores).
